Falco Runtime Security (container threat detection)

            

                Falco watches kernel syscalls across every container on this host and flags suspicious runtime
                behaviour — a shell opened inside a container, reads/writes of sensitive files, package installs,
                unexpected outbound connections, privilege escalation and more — using its maintained rule set.
                Each match is pushed here over the internal network. Detection rules live in the Falco container
                (add your own under deploy-configs/falco/rules.d/); below you control what maniwani
                keeps and shows.

                {% if falco.token_set %}ingest token set{% else %}no ingest token — set FALCO_INGEST_TOKEN in .env{% endif %}

Peers

            

                A .b32.i2p host is reached through the I2P SOCKS proxy and never
                reveals this server's address to the peer. Anything else is dialled directly
                over the open internet — which works without an I2P router, and means
                the peer sees your server's IP. The transport is decided by the address, so a
                peer written as I2P can never be contacted in the clear by mistake.

Distance-based image bans (federated)

            

                Ban an image by perceptual fingerprint: any upload or imported image whose
                fingerprint is within the Manhattan-distance threshold is auto-blocked — so re-encoded or
                rescaled near-duplicates are caught, not just byte-identical files. Local bans broadcast to
                peers over the banlist newsgroup; bans learned from peers are applied here too. Use the

NSFW image filter

            

                Every uploaded image is scored 0–1 by
                Yahoo open_nsfw
                running in the nsfw-classifier sidecar, and rejected at or above the
                threshold. Boards carry their own on/off toggle — user-created boards are
                always filtered, only sysop-created boards can opt out.
            

            {% if not nsfw_configured %}
            

                Classifier not configured.
                Set NSFW_CLASSIFIER_URL=http://nsfw-classifier:8000 and start the
                container. Until then images are stored unscored and nothing is rejected.
            

            {% endif %}
            

                

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        
                        
                    

                    

                        

                            
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            
                        

                        

                            
                            
                            
                                open_nsfw only reads still images, so video is checked by
                                pulling one frame through ffmpeg first. Without this, video
                                is stored unscored — scraped video in particular then
                                bypasses the filter entirely. A video whose frame cannot be
                                decoded is allowed through with a warning rather than
                                blocked, so a codec problem cannot stop all video.
                            
                        

                    

                

                

                    
                    
                    
                

            

            
                Lower the threshold to catch more (and produce more false positives); raise it to be
                permissive. 0.80 is a starting point, not a tuned value — check
                it against your own material. Leaving "block uploads when the classifier is down"
                off means a sidecar outage lets images through unscored rather than halting uploads.
